answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents lock collateral in a dedicated vault and publish zero-knowledge proofs over cryptographic attestation chains verifying past execution traces. Each trace verifies a unique hardware relic without leaking telemetry. To mint identities, verification costs scale superlinearly: a baseline saffron staking tier grows exponentially per concurrent identity, ensuring exponential capital exhaustion that makes deploying a Sybil swarm economically fatal.
